De Novo Construction of Substituted T er ephthalates via
Phosphine Catalyzed Domino Benzannulation Reactions
Dan W ang,
a
Junhui Lin,

Abstract: The robustness of phosphine catalysis
enabling the domino benzannulation reactions of
allenoates with enamines is described. A broad array
of substituted terephthalates were delivered under
simple and practical reaction conditions. Further-
more, the reaction could be carried out on a gram
scale with higher yield, and various conversions of
the terephthalate products demonstrate the versatil-
ity of this transformation.
Keywords: T erephthalates; Benzannulation; Alle-
noates; Enamines; Phosphine
T erephthalate structure commonly occurs in molecules
within a diverse array of biological and pharmaceutical
activities, as well as finding significant applications in
polymer materials.
[1]
It is noteworthy that the global
consumption of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is
estimated to be 108 million tons in 2020, which will
utilize immense amounts of fossil oil.
[2]
In addition,
introduction of terephthalate-containing systems allows
increasing structural novelty and adding its value as a
versatile building unit in pharmacologically relevant
compounds (Figure 1).
[3]
Given its great prominence,
seeking for eff icient and selective methodologies to
generate substituted terephthalates has remained a
perennial interest. In principle, a conjugated diene and
an alkene may enable direct access to p-Xylene via
Diels-Alder reaction and dehydrogenation sequence,
which need further oxidation to aff ord terephthalate.
[4]
Pleasantly , Xu’ s group proposed a synthetic route to
diethyl terephthalate (DET), using biomass-derived
muconic acid, ethanol, and ethylene as the reactants,
through a cascade process combining esterification,
Diels-Alder cycloaddition and dehydrogenation
(Scheme 1a).
[5]
Whereas, more rigorous conditions are
still required to proceed this protocol. Alternatively ,
transition-metal-catalyzed methods have long proven
to be valuable for transferring functional group to
precursor substrates.
[6]
For instance, Ritter ’ s group
showcased Ru-catalyzed C � H amination, leading to
amino-substituted terephthalate (Scheme 1a).
[7]
Ben-
zannulation was also pursued vigorously as a straight-
forward approach to polysubstituted aromatic
compounds.
[8]
Among of those, transition-metal cata-
lysts have demonstrated great potentials to carry out
the preparation of functionalized benzenes. In recent
advances, Moret’ s group achieved [2 + 2 + 2] cyclo-
trimerization with the use of Ni(0) complexes,
selectively affor ding carboxylate substituted terephtha-
lates from terminal alkynes (Scheme 1a).
[9]
Although a
small number of such methods have been exploited,
multistep strategies and restriction on the substitution

[10]
From the viewpoint of diversity-oriented synthesis,
developing fundamentally distinct methods for the
construction of terephthalates in efficient but simple
manner is still in great demand as we deem necessary ,
but remains a significant challenge.
Despite phosphine-catalyzed annulation of alle-
noates has become one of the most eff icient strategy
for construction of cyclic compounds,
[1 1]
only one
benzannulation event occurred in 41% yield when
involving β’-acetoxy allenotes.
[12]
As readily accessible
feedstocks, enamines often serve as versatile reactive
intermediates for granting a direct access to cyclization
products due to their intrinsically tempered
nucleophilicity .
[13]
Since a benzannulation-reaction-
based approach to generate substituted terephthalates
has not been exploited thus far , continuing our on-
going research utilizing the reactivity β’-acetoxy
allenoates,
[14]
we designed a convenient alternative
protocol for the de novo construction of terephthalate
architecture via phosphine catalyzed benzannulation
reaction of enamines and allenoates (Scheme 1b).
Notably , terephthalate molecules possessing diverse
ester groups, which are otherwise challenging to
synthesize, could be precisely prepared under our
reaction condition. In addition, this elegant strategy
constitute a credible transform leading to biphenyl
skeletons, versatile building blocks in synthetic or ganic
chemistry .
Exploratory studies began with the [4 + 2] annula-
tion of ethyl (Z)-2-((4-methylphenyl)sulfonamido)-3-
phenylacrylate (1 a) and benzyl 2-(acetoxymethyl)buta-
2,3-dienoate (2 a) as model substrates(T able 1). Ex-
pectedly , preliminary assessment with typical
phosphine was found to be very encouraging, which
produced the desired 5- benzyl 2-ethyl [1, 1’-biphen-
yl]-2, 5-dicarboxylate (3 aa) in moderate yield when
the reaction completed within five hours (entry 1).

Having identified the optimal reaction conditions,
we sought to investigate the diversity of this reaction
(T able 2). By switching to aryl ring substituted
enamine, moderate conversion was acquired (3 ba).
Due to the steric hindrance of ester groups substituted
enamines, replacing the substitution pattern with
aliphatic substitution on the aryl ring turned out to be
competent, while the aryl substituted derivatives
showed lower reactivity toward this transformation
(3 ca, 3 da and 3 ea). It is worth noting that the
presence of halogen substituents on the aryl rings has a
considerable impact on the eff iciency of this reaction,
furnished the corresponding products (3 fa–3 ka) with
synthetically useful outcomes. Although the yield of
the ortho-chloro substituted product 3 ka is lower than
the meta and para substituential products 3 ga and
3 ha, the ortho-halogen substituted aromatic ring
system is relatively diff icult to be prepared by other
methods. Substituent including strong electron with-
drawing group CF
3
on the aryl ring of substrate 1 was
also well tolerated, furnishing the corresponding 3 la in
high yields (83%). Ester -substituted enamine 1 m was
also compatible for this reaction, and generated 3 ma
in excellent yield (93%). Unfortunately , when com-
pound 1 n with p-OMe substitutent on the aromatic
ring was used as the substrate, the benzannulation
product 3 na couldn’t be obtained. The attempts to try
other enamines, e. g. alkyl substituted enamines, aryl
substituted enamines with SMe, CF
3
, NO
2

the aromatic ring, all failed, because the starting

confirmed by single crystal X-ray dif fraction analysis

aryl-bearing substitution on allenoates, all underwent
the annulation reaction successfully to affor d the
corresponding products in acceptable yields (3 ab–
3 af). Pleasingly , the catalytic protocol also proceeded
smoothly when embedding o-fluorobenzyl, o-meth-
ylbenzyl, 1-naphthyl and 9-anthryl in substrates 2,
reflecting the mildness and high efficienc y of this
protocol (3 ag–3 aj).
Since the substrate generality has been well-
established, we thus focused on the further illustration
of the synthetic utilities. Gram experiment was
performed prior to the late-stage diversification, to our
delight, nearly quantitative yield was achieved under
standard conditions (Scheme 2). It should be men-
tioned that presumably steric hindrance led to the
regioselective products both in the hydrolysis and
reduction of 3 ha. Specifically , treatment of 3 ha under
inorg anic basic conditions led to hydrolyzed product.
The following coupling of the corresponding acid to L-
methionine methyl ester hydrochloride enabled access
to 4, which can be further transformed to farnesyl-
transferase inhibitors.
[17]
Additionally , the reduction
proceeded well when LiAlH
4
was employed, giving
product 5 in 75% yield. Furthermore, 5-benzyl 2-
methyl 4’-bromo-[1,1’-biphenyl]-2,5-dicarboxylates
(3 ha) allowed for post-transformation modification
and afforded the Suzuki-coupling product 6.
Deuterium experiment was conducted to elucidate
the further mechanism of this reaction (see the
Supporting Information for more details). All else
being equal, 20 equiv . of D
2
O was introduced into the
reaction system. Incorporation of deuterium in the
corresponding positions was observed, clearly indicat-
ing that intermediates with the carbanion involved in
the benzannulation reaction.
Supported by preliminary mechanistic studies com-
bined with precedent literatures, a tentative mechanism
for the current benzannulation reaction is proposed
(Scheme 3). 1,2-elimination of the acetate group
followed by the phosphine’ s nucleophilic attack of
phosphine at allenoate 1 a released the intermediate A,
which exhibited electrophilicity and next served as a
four -carbon reacting partner for the catalytic annula-
tion reaction. W ith the help of base, enamine interacted
with A leading to intermediate C. Then, intermediate
G was delivered undergo ing 1,2-elimination followed
by intramolecular addition and proton transfer process.
Finally , the aromaticity is constructed after deprotona-
tion and isomerization to aff ord the benzannulation
product 3 a, along with the regeneration of phosphine
catalyst.
In summary , we reported on the discovery of a
strategically distinct approach to substituted terephtha-
lates via domino benzannulation of β’-acetoxy alle-
noates and enamines by environmentally friendly
conditions and commercially available phosphine cata-
lyst, which can be drove with synthetically useful
yields. This protocol features a broad substrate scope
and attractively mild conditions. Additionally , the late-
stage functionalization illustrated the synthetic utility .

Abstract: The robustness of phosphine catalysis
enabling the domino benzannulation reactions of
allenoates with enamines is described. A broad array
of substituted terephthalates were delivered under
simple and practical reaction conditions. Further-
more, the reaction could be carried out on a gram
scale with higher yield, and various conversions of
the terephthalate products demonstrate the versatil-
ity of this transformation.
Keywords: T erephthalates; Benzannulation; Alle-
noates; Enamines; Phosphine
T erephthalate structure commonly occurs in molecules
within a diverse array of biological and pharmaceutical
activities, as well as finding significant applications in
polymer materials.
[1]
It is noteworthy that the global
consumption of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is
estimated to be 108 million tons in 2020, which will
utilize immense amounts of fossil oil.
[2]
In addition,
introduction of terephthalate-containing systems allows
increasing structural novelty and adding its value as a
versatile building unit in pharmacologically relevant
compounds (Figure 1).
[3]
Given its great prominence,
seeking for eff icient and selective methodologies to
generate substituted terephthalates has remained a
perennial interest. In principle, a conjugated diene and
an alkene may enable direct access to p-Xylene via
Diels-Alder reaction and dehydrogenation sequence,
which need further oxidation to aff ord terephthalate.
[4]
Pleasantly , Xu’ s group proposed a synthetic route to
diethyl terephthalate (DET), using biomass-derived
muconic acid, ethanol, and ethylene as the reactants,
through a cascade process combining esterification,
Diels-Alder cycloaddition and dehydrogenation
(Scheme 1a).
[5]
Whereas, more rigorous conditions are
still required to proceed this protocol. Alternatively ,
transition-metal-catalyzed methods have long proven
to be valuable for transferring functional group to
precursor substrates.
[6]
For instance, Ritter ’ s group
showcased Ru-catalyzed C � H amination, leading to
amino-substituted terephthalate (Scheme 1a).
[7]
Ben-
zannulation was also pursued vigorously as a straight-
forward approach to polysubstituted aromatic
compounds.
[8]
Among of those, transition-metal cata-
lysts have demonstrated great potentials to carry out
the preparation of functionalized benzenes. In recent
advances, Moret’ s group achieved [2 + 2 + 2] cyclo-
trimerization with the use of Ni(0) complexes,
selectively affor ding carboxylate substituted terephtha-
lates from terminal alkynes (Scheme 1a).
[9]
Although a
small number of such methods have been exploited,
multistep strategies and restriction on the substitution

[10]
From the viewpoint of diversity-oriented synthesis,
developing fundamentally distinct methods for the
construction of terephthalates in efficient but simple
manner is still in great demand as we deem necessary ,
but remains a significant challenge.
Despite phosphine-catalyzed annulation of alle-
noates has become one of the most eff icient strategy
for construction of cyclic compounds,
[1 1]
only one
benzannulation event occurred in 41% yield when
involving β’-acetoxy allenotes.
[12]
As readily accessible
feedstocks, enamines often serve as versatile reactive
intermediates for granting a direct access to cyclization
products due to their intrinsically tempered
nucleophilicity .
[13]
Since a benzannulation-reaction-
based approach to generate substituted terephthalates
has not been exploited thus far , continuing our on-
going research utilizing the reactivity β’-acetoxy
allenoates,
[14]
we designed a convenient alternative
protocol for the de novo construction of terephthalate
architecture via phosphine catalyzed benzannulation
reaction of enamines and allenoates (Scheme 1b).
Notably , terephthalate molecules possessing diverse
ester groups, which are otherwise challenging to
synthesize, could be precisely prepared under our
reaction condition. In addition, this elegant strategy
constitute a credible transform leading to biphenyl
skeletons, versatile building blocks in synthetic or ganic
chemistry .

Since the substrate generality has been well-
established, we thus focused on the further illustration
of the synthetic utilities. Gram experiment was
performed prior to the late-stage diversification, to our
delight, nearly quantitative yield was achieved under
standard conditions (Scheme 2). It should be men-

regioselective products both in the hydrolysis and
reduction of 3 ha. Specifically , treatment of 3 ha under
inorg anic basic conditions led to hydrolyzed product.
The following coupling of the corresponding acid to L-
methionine methyl ester hydrochloride enabled access
to 4, which can be further transformed to farnesyl-
transferase inhibitors.
[17]
Additionally , the reduction
proceeded well when LiAlH
4
was employed, giving
product 5 in 75% yield. Furthermore, 5-benzyl 2-
methyl 4’-bromo-[1,1’-biphenyl]-2,5-dicarboxylates
(3 ha) allowed for post-transformation modification
and afforded the Suzuki-coupling product 6.
Deuterium experiment was conducted to elucidate
the further mechanism of this reaction (see the
Supporting Information for more details). All else
being equal, 20 equiv . of D
2
O was introduced into the
reaction system. Incorporation of deuterium in the
corresponding positions was observed, clearly indicat-
ing that intermediates with the carbanion involved in
the benzannulation reaction.
Supported by preliminary mechanistic studies com-
bined with precedent literatures, a tentative mechanism
for the current benzannulation reaction is proposed
(Scheme 3). 1,2-elimination of the acetate group
followed by the phosphine’ s nucleophilic attack of
phosphine at allenoate 1 a released the intermediate A,
which exhibited electrophilicity and next served as a
four -carbon reacting partner for the catalytic annula-
tion reaction. W ith the help of base, enamine interacted
with A leading to intermediate C. Then, intermediate
G was delivered undergo ing 1,2-elimination followed
by intramolecular addition and proton transfer process.
Finally , the aromaticity is constructed after deprotona-
tion and isomerization to aff ord the benzannulation
product 3 a, along with the regeneration of phosphine
catalyst.
In summary , we reported on the discovery of a
strategically distinct approach to substituted terephtha-
lates via domino benzannulation of β’-acetoxy alle-
noates and enamines by environmentally friendly
conditions and commercially available phosphine cata-
lyst, which can be drove with synthetically useful
yields. This protocol features a broad substrate scope
and attractively mild conditions. Additionally , the late-
stage functionalization illustrated the synthetic utility .
